hook.text: Japan sits on four tectonic plates. Stopping a bullet train before the shaking hits is life or death.

buildup.text: Seismic sensors along the coast detect earthquakes seconds before the waves reach inland rail lines.

discovery.text: Those few seconds are enough. Automatic systems cut power and apply brakes before the train feels anything.

twist.text: In 2011, during the massive Tohoku earthquake, Shinkansen trains stopped safely. No derailments occurred.

climax.text: This system has been adopted by other countries, including Taiwan and parts of California.

punchline.text: Seconds of warning save hundreds of lives.

quiz.question: How does Japan's earthquake early warning system protect bullet trains?
options: Sensors trigger automatic braking before shaking arrives
